answer: Make identity expensive in time, not money: every new agent must crack a slow, useful puzzle — verifying a shard of real network data — before it can transact. The work is layered like shale, each step cheap alone but heavy in bulk, and the puzzle difficulty adapts so a single machine can mint only a few identities a day. A walnut-hard shell of compute around each account means a sybil farmer faces a karst of caverns to dig through: ten thousand clones need ten thousand real workdays, while one honest agent passes once and keeps its standing.
